README: A whole-piece reading: every mark an edition prints for one fugue, in every voice and bar, attached to the game's own notes.

Notes are addressed as in data/touch/pieces.json: v = voice index (here 0 Soprano, 1 Alto, 2 Tenor, 3 Bass, pieces.json voiceNames), on = onset tick (tpq 1920; a 4/4 bar is 7680 ticks; bar n starts at (n-1)*7680). p (MIDI) and name are a check (names are the game's spelling, even where the edition renotates), bar and pos (sixteenths from the barline) are for people.

marks[]: one note's articulation. art is one of staccato (dot), wedge (Keil: shorter and sharper), tenuto (dash: full value, a slight lean), portato (dash over dot: held a little apart, each note weighted), accent (>), marcato (^ over a dot: struck hard and left), fermata. A note may have two marks (wedge+tenuto).

slurs[]: spans in one voice, from and to both included. kind "slur" = a group played as one gesture (joined inside, the last note lighter and, with lastShort, let go early); kind "portato" = dots under a slur (each note detached a little but carried in one line); kind "phrase" = a long phrasing arc over a whole subject or line. role says what the slur covers.
dyn[]: a printed level at a time, for the voices it was printed for (Busoni prints dynamics per staff, sometimes per voice).

hairpins[]: cresc/dim spans in time for the given voices. text[]: words printed in the score with an English gloss. tempo.changes[] is left empty on purpose: the owner has ruled out tempo warping except at fermatas, so Busoni's tempo words are kept only in tempo.notes[] (applied: false) and fermatas stay in marks[].

breaths[]: a printed caesura before a note. voicing[]: pianistic re-voicings, recorded as notes only and not to be applied: octave-doubling (interval in semitones) and added notes. ornaments[]: a printed ornament and how Busoni realises it.
rules[]: instructions that apply to unmarked notes; the game must apply these by rule. sections[]: Busoni's double bars.
fingering: a summary of patterns and a few samples (fingers in the order of the notes from that note on); not every digit is transcribed.
footnotes[]: German text (as printed, old spelling kept) and an English translation.
conf on every item: sure (clearly printed and placed), likely (printed, the placement or the sign read from a 300 dpi scan with some doubt), unsure (a guess: hard to see, or inferred).
This format is a superset of docs/wtc/readings/*.json: the old per-note subject marks can be derived from marks[] and slurs[] on the first entry.
title: Fugue 7 in E♭ major, BWV 876

edition.author: Ferruccio B. Busoni
edition.title: Das wohltemperirte Clavier, Erster Theil, bearbeitet … von Ferruccio B. Busoni (this Book II fugue is printed there as Fuga VII)
edition.swap: Busoni swapped the two E-flat fugues: Book II's fugue (BWV 876) stands as No. VII of his Book I volume, and Book I's (BWV 852) as "Fuga VII*" in his Book II volume. This reading is Book II's fugue from the Book I volume.

character: "Wuchtig, sehr gehalten / Pesante e ben tenuto, ma non legato" (b.1); a quiet middle section, "dolce, tranquillo e tutto legato" (b.46), called a resting point in footnote 2; "f come prima" at the return (b.59).
dynamicPlan: f for each entry of the exposition (bass b.1, tenor b.7); soprano answer marcato (b.21); cresc. into the double bar (b.28); meno f e più legato (b.30); alto meno f (b.37); dim. (b.45) into dolce tranquillo (b.46); tenor marcato ma dolce (b.53); cresc. (b.56–58) to f come prima (b.59); cresc. ed allarg. (b.65) to ff with fermatas (b.70).

slurs.role: dotted figure (starts on a tied note)
runs on over the page turn

dyn.role: printed as a word with the character text

text.text: Wuchtig, sehr gehalten. / Pesante e ben tenuto, ma non legato
text.en: weighty, very held back; heavy and well sustained, but not legato
entry label in brackets: the alto carries the line
soprano entry: loud, as at the start

rules.art: non legato: each quarter and half held well but lifted (ben tenuto, ma non legato)
as at the start (come prima): weighty, non legato

sections.en: end of the exposition (Busoni's section I)
into the soprano entry, f come prima (section III)

pedalNote: No pedal marks in the main text.

footnotes.de: Die mehr scherzhafte Fuge, die ursprünglich diesen Platz einnimmt, steht im ausgesprochenen Missverhältniss zu dem … Praeludium … Dagegen zeigt die Es dur-Fuge aus dem zweiten Bande … eine auffallende Affinität …
footnotes.en: The swap: Book I's more playful E-flat fugue is out of proportion to its grand prelude, so Busoni prints Book II's E-flat fugue here; Book I's fugue goes into his Book II volume as "Fuga VII*".

footnotes.de: Hier begegnen wir dem seltenen Beispiele, dass der II. Abschnitt des Durchführungstheiles einen Ruhepunkt verzeichnet …
footnotes.en: Section II (b.46) is a resting point; the counterpoint picks up again in section III at the tenor's signal.

caveats: Transcribed from Busoni's Book I volume (Schirmer 1894), where this Book II fugue stands as No. VII; the Book II volume prints Book I's E-flat fugue in its place.
Busoni labels entries T, B, A, S in the score; these are kept in text[] as entry labels.
Ties are not recorded; most arcs in the upper staff of b.46–68 are ties over the long notes and are left out.
Footnote 3 (pdf 48) is an ossia for b.59–70 with the bass doubled in octaves and pedal: skipped (ossia, octave doubling).
Read from 200 dpi crops, zoomed to 300–400 dpi where needed; the scan is a 1-bit image.
